papers.title: Kondo Lattice model for field induced triplet pairing in CeRh$_2$As$_2$
papers.abstract: Spin triplet superconductors are of interest because of their topological properties, and their robustness to high magnetic fields. CeRh$_2$As$_2$ is a unique heavy fermion superconductor with both even-parity and candidate odd-parity superconducting phases with a special feature enabling a field induced phase transition between the two. The field induced transition which switches the parity of the Cooper pairs is enabled by a staggered antisymmetric spin orbit coupling (ASOC) interaction. However, the heavy fermion origins of the superconductivity in CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and the origin of the antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling are currently unexplored. Here, we develop a Kondo lattice model for CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and demonstrate how local hybridization between Cerium $d$- and $f$-orbitals, driven by the locally broken inversion symmetry, at the Cerium sites generates the ASOC. The resulting Kondo lattice model leads to nearly degenerate even and odd parity superconducting states that display a field induced parity transition between an even-parity state and an odd-parity pseudospin triplet state. We discuss the wider implications of our results extended to other heavy fermion systems like CeSiI.
papers.finding: Using a Kondo lattice model with local d-f hybridization, the study finds that locally broken inversion symmetry generates the antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling, producing nearly degenerate even- and odd-parity superconducting states with a field-induced parity transition.

papers.title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
papers.abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures ($T_{\text{c}}$), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO$_2$ plane -- as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) -- and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record $T_{\text{c}}$ of Bi2223.
papers.finding: Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, the study finds that the underdoped inner CuO2 plane of Bi2223 hosts charge order yet exceptional quasiparticle coherence, while overdoped outer planes show enhanced gaps, indicating an interlayer mechanism optimizing both pairing and coherence.

papers.title: Avalanches and Aging Driven by Parametric Amplification in Kerr Oscillator Networks
papers.abstract: Gain, loss, and nonlinearity shape the phase-space landscape of driven-dissipative systems, such as Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO) networks realized in superconducting, nanomechanical, and photonic arrays. Networks of KPOs exploit the stationary states of this landscape for Ising machines, bosonic error-correcting codes, and sensing. Yet how transients reach these states from a given initial condition remains largely unexplored. Here we show that KPO networks with nonlinear couplings can develop avalanches in their transient dynamics: rapid cascades of amplification between modes reminiscent of the relaxation avalanches of glassy systems. The mechanism is that parametric gain first activates the modes whose detuning it can overcome, and their nonlinear frequency shifts then pull dormant modes into the gain window one at a time. Dormant modes keep decaying while they wait for their turn, so every activation starts from a smaller seed and the intervals between activations grow geometrically. The network thus ages: the longer it has evolved, the slower it changes, and activations accumulate only logarithmically in time. In a 20-mode network, each dwell lasts about twice as long as the previous one. While aging delays the approach to the stationary state, additive noise sets a floor on the seeds and unsticks the network, shortening the longest dwells first while the activation sequence survives to noise several orders of magnitude stronger.
papers.finding: Using Kerr parametric oscillator networks with nonlinear couplings, the study finds transient avalanches in which parametric gain activates modes sequentially, causing the network to age with dwell times growing geometrically—about twice as long each time in a 20-mode network.

papers.title: Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking in the Centrosymmetric Nonsymmorphic Superconductor RuB2
papers.abstract: Centrosymmetric nonsymmorphic AB2 (A = Ru, Os) borides exhibit anomalous superconducting properties, but the microscopic nature of their superconducting ground state remains unresolved. Here, we investigate RuB2 using zero- and transverse-field muon spin relaxation (muSR), first-principles electronic-structure calculations, and Ginzburg-Landau symmetry analysis. Zero-field muSR reveals spontaneous internal magnetic fields below Tc = 1.6 K, providing direct evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB). Transverse-field measurements establish a fully gapped superconducting state, with a gap magnitude close to the BCS weak-coupling limit. Density-functional calculations show that RuB2 is a multiband Z2 topological metal with appreciable spin-orbit coupling. Guided by the experimental observations and the symmetry of the orthorhombic crystal structure, our Ginzburg-Landau analysis suggests that an internally antisymmetric, nonunitary spin-triplet state is a promising candidate for the superconducting order parameter. This candidate is consistent with both the observed TRSB and the fully gapped superconducting state. These results establish RuB2 as a promising platform for investigating unconventional superconductivity arising from the interplay of crystal symmetry, multiband electronic structure, and spin-orbit coupling, and motivate further studies of related nonsymmorphic borides. The two muSR measurements provide complementary constraints: zero-field data probe spontaneous magnetism associated with TRSB, while transverse-field data characterize superconducting field distribution and support a full gap. The topological electronic structure and spin-orbit coupling provide context for unconventional pairing. Although these results do not uniquely determine the order parameter, they narrow candidates and highlight that nonsymmorphic symmetry may shape superconductivity in RuB2.
papers.finding: Using zero- and transverse-field muon spin relaxation, the study finds spontaneous internal magnetic fields below Tc = 1.6 K indicating time-reversal symmetry breaking, alongside a fully gapped state consistent with a nonunitary spin-triplet order parameter.

papers.title: Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Transitions on a Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Mixed quantum states can exhibit unconventional forms of symmetry breaking without pure-state counterparts. A prominent example is strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB), which cannot be diagnosed by observables linear in the density matrix. Here, we experimentally resolve finite-size critical signatures of SW-SSB transitions on a superconducting quantum processor. We develop a measurement protocol that combines quantum measurements with classical processing based on the known dephasing channel to reconstruct nonlinear mixed-state correlators. Using only two measurement settings, the protocol reconstructs fidelity, Rényi-2, and linear correlators, as well as string observables. Applying this approach to matrix-product states subjected to power-law-correlated dephasing, we observe finite-size crossings and scaling collapses in nonlinear correlators, accompanied by decaying linear correlations. We further map the estimated SW-SSB transition points across initial-state and channel parameters. Measurements of linear and Rényi-2 string observables further reveal signatures of mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases, with a nonlinear string-order crossover aligned with an independently estimated SW-SSB transition point. Our results establish a quantum-classical approach to probing SW-SSB critical behavior and mixed-state SPT order.
papers.finding: Using a quantum-classical protocol on a superconducting quantum processor that reconstructs nonlinear mixed-state correlators, the study finds finite-size crossings and scaling collapses diagnosing strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions.

papers.title: Phonon-dominated thermal conductivity of a superconducting amorphous MoSi thin film
papers.abstract: We use the differential 3ω method to directly measure the temperature dependent thermal conductivity for about 90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 thin films. The measurements are performed in a closed-cycle cryostat to access the temperature range between 50 K and 300 K. The MoSi thin films are capped with Al2O3 and probed with a Pt wire. The results show that the thermal conductivity does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law. This implies that thermal transport in MoSi is not dominated by electrons but by phonon-like excitations, contrary to what is assumed in many electro-thermal models of superconducting devices. We argue that this property might be related to the weak localization visible in the resistivity as a function of temperature curves of the superconductor.
papers.finding: Using the differential 3ω method, the study finds that the thermal conductivity of ~90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 films does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law, implying thermal transport is dominated by phonon-like excitations rather than electrons.

papers.title: Altermagnetic Control of Charge-4e Superconductivity
papers.abstract: We show that a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconducting islands coupled by altermagnetic Josephson junctions supports an independent charge-4e phase. Tuning the altermagnetic splitting suppresses the leading single-pair tunneling harmonic while retaining strong double-pair coupling, producing a finite charge-4e region between staggered and uniform charge-2e states. Using the complete temperature-dependent microscopic Josephson spectrum, we find short-range ordinary pair correlations alongside algebraic coherence of pairs of Cooper pairs. Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless scaling and a half-flux response further identify the charge-4e phase. Our results establish altermagnetism as a microscopic means to select between ordinary and composite superconducting coherence.
papers.finding: Using a two-dimensional classical array of conventional superconducting islands coupled by altermagnetic Josephson junctions, the study finds an independent charge-4e phase with algebraic coherence of Cooper-pair pairs.

papers.title: Sideband fingerprints of antibunched light in cascaded quantum wave mixing
papers.abstract: Quantum wave mixing on a single superconducting qubit produces a hierarchy of coherent side peaks associated with elastic multiphoton scattering pathways. In a cascaded source--probe geometry these pathways become sensitive to the photon statistics of the radiation emitted by the source qubit. We develop an analytical theory of this effect starting from the cascaded master equation in the weak-driving regime. In the coherent-filtering limit when the decay rate of the probe qubit is less than that of the source, the standard coherent--coherent wave-mixing hierarchy is recovered. In the opposite limit, side peaks associated with multiphoton absorption from the antibunched source field are parametrically suppressed. Numerical solutions confirm the analytical scaling laws. The resulting sideband hierarchy provides a frequency-domain fingerprint of antibunched itinerant microwave light.
papers.finding: Using an analytical theory of cascaded wave mixing starting from the cascaded master equation, the study finds that side peaks from multiphoton absorption of antibunched source radiation are parametrically suppressed when probe decay exceeds source decay.

papers.title: Surface-extended Andreev bound states emerging from intrinsic surface superconductivity of PtBi$_2$
papers.abstract: Intrinsic topological superconductivity remains one of the central open questions in condensed-matter physics. The three-dimensional Weyl semimetal PtBi$_2$ has recently been shown by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to host a superconducting gap that opens exclusively on its Fermi-arc surface states and exhibits a nodal structure, making it a promising platform for exploring unconventional and potentially topological superconductivity. However, despite these momentum-resolved insights, the real-space spectroscopic signatures of unconventional superconductivity in PtBi$_2$ remain unclear. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we reveal a sizable and spatially homogeneous gap ($Δ> 10\,\mathrm{meV}$) on atomically pristine terraces of PtBi$_2$. Within this gap, we detect surface-extended in-gap states exhibiting pronounced atomic-scale spatial modulation. Analysis of the tunneling spectra indicates that these states are most consistently interpreted as Andreev bound states within a superconducting gap. Further phenomenological modeling shows that their characteristic spectral features are naturally captured by a chiral pairing scenario. Our results establish a direct real-space connection between the superconducting gap and surface-extended quasiparticle states in PtBi$_2$, and provide new insight into the nature of its unconventional surface superconductivity. These findings highlight PtBi$_2$ as a versatile platform for exploring exotic quasiparticle excitations and potential Majorana physics.
papers.finding: Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, the study finds a sizable, spatially homogeneous gap (Δ > 10 meV) on PtBi2 terraces with surface-extended in-gap states interpreted as Andreev bound states within a chiral pairing scenario.

papers.title: Effects of Nonmagnetic Impurities on Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions in Microwave-Driven Superconductors
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium steady states of a microwave-driven BCS superconductor in the presence of nonmagnetic impurity scattering and energy relaxation. Using the Floquet-Nambu-Keldysh Green's function method together with the self-consistent Born approximation, we self-consistently determine the superconducting order parameter in the microwave-driven steady state. We find that the nonequilibrium phase diagram depends strongly on the impurity-scattering strength. When impurity scattering is absent or weak, the steady-state order parameter is single-valued at each temperature and drive frequency. At intermediate scattering strengths, we find bistability between microwave-enhanced and microwave-suppressed superconducting states. As the impurity-scattering strength increases further, we instead find bistability between the superconducting and normal states. This evolution reflects competition between two effects of microwave driving: Eliashberg-type enhancement through the redistribution of thermally excited quasiparticles and suppression through pair-breaking-induced quasiparticle generation. In contrast to the robustness of equilibrium $s$-wave superconductivity against nonmagnetic impurity scattering, our results demonstrate that nonmagnetic impurity scattering plays a central role in determining the character of nonequilibrium superconducting phase transitions under microwave driving.
papers.finding: Using the Floquet-Nambu-Keldysh Green's function method with the self-consistent Born approximation, the study finds that the nonequilibrium phase diagram of a microwave-driven BCS superconductor depends strongly on nonmagnetic impurity-scattering strength, including bistability regimes.

papers.title: A chemical avenue to manipulate field-reentrant superconducting rivalries in infinite layer nickelates
papers.abstract: Recently, preliminary magnetic field-reentrant superconductivity manifested in high-temperature (Tc) Eu-doped infinite-layer (IL) nickelates, beyond analogous discoveries exclusively in low-Tc systems. This evokes intriguing fundamental issues about potential quantum-phase boundary and criticality between unconventional superconductivity and field-reentrant-one, which are inexplicable owing to formidable challenges in growing IL-nickelates towards later-series rare-earths. Herein, we open up chemical avenues to enable effective growth of (RE1-yRE'y)1-xEuxNiO2 (RE/RE': Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Dy), giving rise to discoveries of RE-4f-related quantum competition between high-Tc and reentrant superconductivity. Robust magnetic-field-reentrant superconductivity with uniaxial anisotropy is observed at superconducting-dome boundaries, stemming from Eu2+-4f7 associated competition between magnetic-fluctuation promoted pairing and exchange-field interactions. Their quantum-criticality is further modulable via RE(RE')-magnetism, which either reinforces reentrancy or elevates Tc (40.1 K) with more robust critical-current-density (~266 kA/cm2 at 2 K) beyond Sr-/Ca-doped counterparts. Our synthetic route enables the establishment of an ideal platform via IL-nickelates for studying 4f-related unconventional superconductivity and quantum-criticality.
papers.finding: Using growth of (RE1-yRE'y)1-xEuxNiO2 infinite-layer nickelates, the study finds RE-4f-related quantum competition between high-Tc and magnetic-field-reentrant superconductivity, with tunable criticality and Tc up to 40.1 K.

papers.title: Thermal Responses of Spin Density and Spin Current Induced by Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in Proximity Superconductors
papers.abstract: The emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces in s-wave proximity superconducting systems provides a unique platform for generating nontrivial spin responses in the presence of spin-orbit coupling. In this work, we investigate temperature-gradient driven responses of spin polarization and spin current in such a proximity system related to Fe(Te,Se). The interplay of in-plane magnetization, superconductivity, and nematicity gives rise to nontrivial Berry curvature and spin-related hybrid Berry curvature on the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which are shown to lead to finite thermally driven nonequilibrium spin polarization and spin Nernst effect. We find that the responses are strongly enhanced by the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, and are linear in temperature at low temperatures, rendering a unique spintronic character of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces.
papers.finding: Using a theoretical investigation of temperature-gradient driven responses in a Fe(Te,Se)-related s-wave proximity superconducting system, the study finds that Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces strongly enhance thermally driven spin polarization and spin Nernst effect, linear in temperature at low temperatures.
